sources.entry: pypy - A very fast and compliant implementation of the Python language.

summary.one_liner: PyPy is an alternative Python interpreter, written in RPython, that aims to be a fast and compliant implementation of the Python language.
summary.what_it_does: The README is short and mostly points to external documentation, so the details here are limited. It describes PyPy as an interpreter for the Python programming language, built on the RPython compiler framework for dynamic language implementations. It says the source documentation lives in the pypy/doc directory and that there is separate documentation for the RPython framework. It directs users to the project home page and documentation for how to download and use PyPy in place of CPython. It also states that building PyPy from source is time-consuming and resource-intensive, so most users should obtain a prebuilt binary instead.
use_cases: running Python code faster than CPython
developing or contributing to the PyPy interpreter
building a custom Python interpreter with RPython
how_to_run: Download a prebuilt PyPy binary from the project home page or documentation (link not included in the README text)
Building from source is possible but time-consuming and resource-heavy; see the linked build documentation
notable: Interpreter for Python written in RPython, a framework for dynamic language implementations
Positioned as a drop-in alternative to CPython
Documentation source kept in the pypy/doc directory
caveats: Building from source is time-consuming and requires significant computing resources
README is brief and defers most details to external documentation and links not included in the text
